findings.message: The new update copies every changed column into all later periods without checking whether a later period already sets that column itself. If the changed column is the one a planned step changes (fte, base_salary, next_review, contract, grade), the plan is silently overwritten. The fix only handles the reported case, where an unrelated column (department) carries forward. The variant test covers only a department change, never a change to fte or salary. Fix: copy a column into a later period only where that period's value still equals the old in-force value (cur[col]). Otherwise reject the change or ask the caller to choose. Extend the table test with an fte change ahead of an fte step and a salary change ahead of a planned raise.
findings.scenario: A part-timer is at 0.5 FTE with the fixture step to 1.0 on 2026-12-01. HR runs changePerson(fte 0.6, effectiveOn 2026-11-01). The December period becomes 0.6 and the planned full-time step is lost, so allocations capacity is wrong from December. A salary raise from November overwrites a planned January raise in the same way.

findings.message: The previous blocker named four contract reads. This diff fixed only one (getEmployment). getPerson, listPeople and listEmploymentPeriods still take no viewer and apply no data scope or hr:read check. architecture.md requires cross-module reads to 'apply the caller's data scope'. The new header comment calls them safe because they return no classified field, but that does not scope them. Any module can list every person in every legal entity, including leavers with their leave dates, for a user who has no hr:read or is scoped to one entity. Fix: take the caller's Viewer (or ServiceContext) in every contract read and filter by legal-entity scope, as getEmployment now does.
findings.scenario: A chat or MCP tool in another module, acting for a PM who has no HR scope over the AU entity, calls listPeople(tx, { status: ['left'] }). It gets every AU leaver with left dates and managers.

findings.message: With the 'system' reader removed, the contract offers no way for trusted, viewer-less code to read pay. The comment and README tell payroll to 'add its own audited system read'. Under the module standard, payroll may not read hr.employment directly (imports limited to other modules' contracts.ts; reads go through contract functions). So the documented path either breaks the boundary law or leaves payroll with no data. Fix: give the contract an explicit, audited system read that requires an actor core issues (for example a job/system ServiceContext checked like inScope), and document that instead.
findings.scenario: The payroll monthly workflow runs as a job context with no Viewer. getEmployment needs a Viewer, so the run cannot get base_salary or bank_account through the contract. Following the README means querying hr.employment, which check-graph rejects.

findings.message: The SQL fragment is now shared, but the as-of date is still not, so the earlier clock finding was only partly fixed. peopleStats takes a JS Date and derives `now` itself. listDirectory, getPerson, listPeople, reportUserIds and getPersonView call today() inside, with no parameter. PeoplePage passes its own `new Date()` to peopleStats while the directory calls today() separately, and tests can pin the date for stats but not for the directory. Fix: pass one as-of date through every read (directory, contract reads, stats), defaulting once at the entry point.
findings.scenario: In a test, peopleStats(viewer, TODAY=2026-10-16) is compared with listDirectory on the real 2026-10-17. Someone whose new period starts 2026-10-17 counts in the old department on the chart but shows the new one in the directory.

findings.message: recordLeaver now hard-deletes later employment periods (planned FTE steps, raises, or a joiner's whole employment). The audit records only `before: { status }`, so the deleted rows (salary, grade, FTE, dates) are not in any audit record and cannot be restored if the leaver was recorded by mistake. The module standard requires every write to be audited. Fix: put the deleted periods in the audit `before`, or end and void them instead of deleting.
findings.scenario: HR records LL-0417 as leaving 2026-12-31 by mistake (wrong employee number). The planned 2027-02-01 period with its salary and FTE is deleted. The audit row shows only status active→active, and nothing can restore the period.

findings.message: applyStatusDates is a defineService with action hr:person:update, but it never calls inScope and it updates every person in the tenant. Today only the job calls it. Any future caller with an HR viewer scoped to one entity would change statuses in all entities. Fix: call inScope per row, or assert ctx.actor.kind === 'system'.

The rule 'contract end = last period's ends_on' is now written twice: the getEmployment contract_ends_on subquery and the stats `not exists later` clause. ends_on also still carries the leave date set by recordLeaver. As a result, a fixed-term person who resigns next month is counted in contractsEndingNextMonth as an expiring contract.

Statuses move at 00:05 UTC, but people's dates are local. A Sri Lankan joiner (UTC+5:30) stays 'joining' until 05:35 local on their first day, and the status column disagrees with the date-based employmentAt reads until the job runs. The today-only check for person fields also compares against the UTC date, so a LK user just after local midnight who passes their own today is rejected.

The tests hard-code 2026/2027 dates but run against the real clock through today(). For example, the status test expects 2027-01-04 to still be 'joining' and the 2027-01-08 leaver to still be 'active'. These cases will start failing on their own once those dates pass. Pin the clock or derive the dates from today().

An entity's URL code depends on how many entities share its country. Adding a second LK entity silently changes the existing `/hr/e/lk` from a working page to a 404. Give each entity a stable unique code.
